newsitem.title: FINLAND: PAPER'S LAHTEENMAKI SEES NEED FOR BRANCH TALKS.
newsitem.headline: PAPER'S LAHTEENMAKI SEES NEED FOR BRANCH TALKS.

text.p: Finnish paper workers' union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki said on Friday that there would be a need for special branch talks between his union and paper industry employers in connection with pay talks in the autumn.

"The right time to start to work on the pay deal is in the autumn when the economic outlook for next year has become more precise and the government has presented its budget proposal," Lahteenmaki said in the prepared text of a speech.
"In many branches, also in the paper industry, we must then also consider the models by which branch-specific problems can best be solved," he said, but did not elaborate.
Lahteenmaki is widely regarded as one of the most influential branch union leaders in the 1.1-million mainly blue-collar member Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).
He said the current two-year nation-wide low-pay-rise incomes settlement had been disappointing so far from the point of view of employment.
He added, however, that purchasing power had developed favourably.
The current settlement expires in February 1998.
